newsitem.title: USA: Cold, snow impede livestock movement in US Plains.
newsitem.headline: Cold, snow impede livestock movement in US Plains.

text.p: Bitterly cold weather and snow drifts in the northern U.S. Plains and the upper Midwest were hindering livestock movement early Tuesday, and forecasters were calling for more frigid weather.
"We have some more cold weather moving in right now, but it won't be as cold as the last bit of weather," said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp. in Lexington, Mass.
Low temperatures on Tuesday will range from five to six degrees Fahrenheit below zero to one to two degrees above in north central and western Kansas, Burgio said.
Livestock dealers reported windchill readings of 30 degrees below zero in St. Joseph, Mo., 43 below zero in Sioux City, Iowa and 43 degrees below in Sioux Falls, S.D.
"You cannot get the hogs in," one South Dakota dealer said. "Roads are treacherous in northern Iowa and southern Minnesota," he said.
Dealers also reported that heavy snow drifts in northern and western South Dakota and southern Minnesota had snarled traffic and made it nearly impossible to travel.
Light snow was expected to develop Wednesday and Thursday in northern Kansas and accumulations were expected to total one to four inches, forecasters said.
Iowa, northern Missouri and central and northern Illinois could also see as much as two to four inches of snow beginning Wednesday morning, Burgio said.
Temperatures should gradually warm during beginning December 27 through the 30, said Fred Gesser, chief meteorologist with Weather Express in Omaha, Neb.

Until this weekend, temperatures will really be staying where they are," Gesser said. "We'll attempt a warm-up Friday, Saturday, Sunday for Nebraska, the Texas Panhandle, with highs in upper the 50s low 60s."
